routesElsewhere.goesTo: Admissions — UC-02-01, as well as a visit here.

A visit is never deleted. A refused one stays on the record with its reason (BR-8, E9).

steps.note: One step. The pre-registration and the blocklist are checked **by the system, inside the call** — a barred person is stopped by it, not by whoever happens to be on duty (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A blocklist match is refused and the refusal is written; a possible match stops for the desk to judge; a pass not free, a missing purpose or number, or a host not at this branch logs nothing. Where the host cannot be told, the visit still stands.
plan.atomicity: One write: the visit with the time in, the branch and the pass, and the host told (BR-4, BR-5, BR-6). A refusal on a blocklist match is its own write — a refused visit, with the School Admin and the Principal told (BR-7). Nothing is ever deleted (BR-8).

operations.name: visit.log.in
operations.idempotencyKey: visitor_name + contact_number + pass_id + minute, so a double press does not log one arrival twice
operations.purpose: Log a visitor in, checking the pre-registration and the blocklist, and issue the pass against the visit.

parameters.name: visitor_name
parameters.notes: 2 to 100 characters, as the visitor gives it. Taken as offered — no identification is checked against it, which is why a blocklist match can only ever be possible rather than certain (OQ-5).

parameters.name: contact_number
parameters.notes: The visitor's own number (E2).

parameters.name: host_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. Nobody at this branch matches — the person being visited must be at this branch (E3).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the matching people at this branch with their role.

parameters.notes: The person the visitor has come to see. Only people at this branch are offered (E3). They are told the visitor has arrived (BR-6).

parameters.name: purpose
parameters.notes: 5 to 500 characters. Why they have come, as the visitor said it (E1).

parameters.name: pass_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No pass at this branch carries that number.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the matching pass numbers.

parameters.notes: The numbered pass physically handed over, named by its number (V-014). A pass in circulation is not free (BR-5, BR-9).

parameters.name: pre_registration_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse, and say that no pre-registration matches. Logging them in as unexpected is the desk's call (E6).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming today's expected visitors that match with who registered each.

parameters.notes: Where the visit was pre-registered, the pre-registration it is logged in from — the details are already there and the desk confirms them (BR-2, A1).

parameters.name: possible_match_cleared
parameters.notes: True only where the desk has already been shown a possible blocklist match on this visit and says, in their own words, that they have asked and it is somebody else (BR-11, A3). **Never set by a planner, and never on a first attempt.**

parameters.name: staff_id
parameters.notes: The desk staff member acting. Never from the request — the visitor is not an actor (BR-1).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The visit, what the checks found, and the pass against it.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Open, until the visitor is logged out (UC-29-02).

fields.name: pre_registered
fields.description: Whether the person being visited registered it in advance (BR-2).

fields.name: blocklist_result
fields.description: No match, or a possible match the desk cleared. A barred person never reaches this — they are refused (BR-3, BR-11).

fields.name: blocklist_checked
fields.description: False where no blocklist is configured. The visitor has then **not been checked** and must not be reported as cleared (E5).

fields.name: pass_number
fields.description: The pass issued against the visit, accounted for on the way out (BR-5).

fields.name: branch
fields.description: The branch it was made at (BR-4).

fields.name: host_notified
fields.description: Whether the person being visited was told (BR-6, E8).

errors.meaning: The person being visited is not at this branch.
The name is on the blocklist. Entry is refused.
errors.written: The refusal and its reason, as a refused visit. The School Admin and the Principal are told a barred person attempted entry (BR-7, AC-5).
errors.notWritten: No visit is opened and no pass is issued.
errors.note: A refusal stays on the record and is never deleted (BR-8).

errors.meaning: The name is a possible match against the blocklist, not a certain one.
errors.note: On the screen the possible match is shown and the desk carries on (BR-11, A3), and the use case writes no exception for it. A plan cannot pause while the desk asks the visitor, so it stops here: the desk either logs them in again with possible_match_cleared, or refuses them with visit.refuse.

errors.meaning: No blocklist is configured, so the visitor has not been checked.
errors.note: Reported, never passed over — a visitor logged in unchecked must not read as a visitor cleared (AC-10).

errors.meaning: The pass is with another visitor and has not been returned, or is outstanding or retired.
errors.note: A pass in circulation is not free (BR-9). Where none is free, the outstanding ones are chased first (A6).

errors.meaning: The person being visited could not be told.
errors.note: Reported so the desk can telephone them.

planningRules.rule: Only the desk logs a visitor in. A request from somebody saying they are the visitor, or asking to log themselves in, has no route — the visitor is not an actor (BR-1, E10).

Never clear a possible match. It is shown to the desk rather than resolved, because a name is not an identity and only the desk can ask (BR-11). Set possible_match_cleared only from the desk's own statement after the match has been put to them — never on a first attempt, and never because the visitor insists.

Never retry a barred visitor — not with another spelling, another number, or the cleared flag. The system stopping them is the whole point of the blocklist: the person on duty should not be the only thing between a barred person and the school (BR-3, E4).
Report an unchecked visitor as unchecked. Where no blocklist is configured the check returns nothing, and a visitor logged in on those terms must never be described as cleared (E5, AC-10).
Never choose the pass. It is the one physically handed over, and the log-out accounts for that pass and no other (BR-5, BR-9).

Log in from the pre-registration where there is one. An expected visitor and an unexpected one are not handled identically — the desk confirms details already there rather than taking them again (BR-2, A1).
A prospective family enquiring is still a visitor here. Log the visit; the inquiry is recorded separately, in admissions (BR-10, A5).

reversal.statement: No capability undoes a visit. It is closed when the visitor leaves — visit.log.out, UC-29-02 — which records a departure, not a mistake. A visit is never deleted (BR-8, E9).

operations.name: visit.refuse

operations.purpose: Record that the desk refused a visitor entry, and why.

parameters.name: visitor_name
parameters.notes: As the visitor gave it.

parameters.name: contact_number
parameters.notes: Where the visitor gave one.

parameters.name: host_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Omit, and record the refusal without a host (E3 applies only to logging in).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the matching people at this branch.

parameters.notes: Who they said they had come to see, where they said.

parameters.name: purpose
parameters.notes: What they said they had come for, where they said.

parameters.name: refusal_reason
parameters.notes: Why entry was refused, in the desk's own words. Recorded whether or not the person was barred (BR-7). The use case lists the field as generated and gives it no length.

parameters.name: staff_id
parameters.notes: The desk staff member acting. Never from the request — the visitor is not an actor (BR-1).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

planningRules.rule: Record the refusal whenever the desk turns somebody away. A barred person turned away is exactly the event the school is asked about afterwards, and one never written down did not happen (BR-7).
Never write the reason. It is the desk's account, and it stays on the record for good (BR-7, BR-8).
Do not record a second refusal where the system already refused on a blocklist match — that one was written when it happened (E4).

reversal.statement: A refusal is never undone or deleted — it stays on the record with its reason (BR-8, E9). A visitor admitted later is a new visit, logged with visit.log.in.
